question.problem: Find $\nabla f(x,y)$ at the point $(1,\pi)$ given that $f(x,y) = (x - y)\cos y.$
question.worked_solution:
First, we find the partial derivatives: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}((x-y)\operatorname{cos}⁡y) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡y \\ {f}_{y}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}((x-y)\operatorname{cos}⁡y) \\  & =-\operatorname{cos}⁡y-(x-y)\operatorname{sin}⁡y\end{aligned}
$$

So, the gradient is

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,f(x,y) & ={f}_{x}(x,y)\text{ }i+{f}_{y}(x,y)\text{ }j \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡y\text{ }i-(\operatorname{cos}⁡y+(x-y)\operatorname{sin}⁡y)\text{ }j.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the gradient at the specified point, we substitute $(x,y)= (1,\pi)$ into the above, which gives

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,f(1,\pi ) & ={f}_{x}(1,\pi )\text{ }i+{f}_{y}(1,\pi )\text{ }j \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi \text{ }i-(\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi +(1-\pi )\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi )\text{ }j \\  & =-i+j.\end{aligned}
$$
